sections.name: Red Bulborb
sections.card:
Summary: The best-known enemy in the series, a big grub-dog with a red back and white spots, called the Spotty Bulborb in the first game and the Red Bulborb in Pikmin 2. It sleeps in the open by day, wakes when it is attacked or when something is carried right next to it, and then lunges at Pikmin and leaders to eat them.
Weak points: Purple Pikmin do serious damage, especially when their landing stuns it. If a lot of Pikmin attack at once, it shakes them off and goes back to trying to eat.
Tips: With an army of at least 30 Pikmin, keep tossing Pikmin onto its back, even if some are shaken off, rather than swarming it. If you wake it by accident, run until it turns around, then make a new pass. With a very small army, wake it and lead it far from where it sleeps; when it walks home and settles down, attacking at that moment gives a few seconds in which it cannot move or bite. In some metal-themed caves you can lead it off the edge by running around a hole in the sublevel.

sections.name: Dwarf Red Bulborb
sections.card:
Summary: A small, common enemy called the Dwarf Red Bulborb in Pikmin 2. It looks like a young bulborb but is really a breadbug copying a bulborb's look. It barks and chases when it spots a leader or Pikmin, bites one Pikmin at a time and chews it slowly, and never strays far from its territory.
Weak points: A single Pikmin thrown onto its back kills it, and its low health means swarming works too. Killing it while it chews frees the Pikmin it caught. Purple Pikmin are exceptionally effective: they steer onto a nearby enemy when thrown, and quick throws at a group stun the whole group and likely kill most of it.
Tips: It is no threat alone; the danger is numbers, or a dwarf standing next to other enemies, so deal with the dwarfs first in a mixed fight. Purples work well on a crowd, as on the eighth sublevel of the Cavern of Chaos. In Pikmin 2 it does not call for help: the scream that wakes a nearby bulborb happens only in the first game. If you lead it past its range it gives up and walks home.

sections.name: Fiery Blowhog
sections.card:
Summary: A pig-like enemy that shoots fire from its red snout, found commonly in Pikmin 2. It wanders a very small patch, turns to face any leader or Pikmin it notices, and breathes a stream of fire. When Pikmin latch on, it bucks them off into the area in front of it and breathes fire there.
Weak points: Purple Pikmin thrown onto it do serious damage and stop it bucking Pikmin off or breathing fire. It is easier to kill in Pikmin 2, so a big group can swarm it straight away. It must breathe in before it breathes out, and it cannot turn or move from the start of that breath until the end, so its flame does not follow anyone who runs away.
Tips: Any Pikmin type can beat it. Pikmin clinging to it cannot be set alight and Red Pikmin ignore fire; the page warns that being bucked into water is what can kill them, so turn it away from water first. In Pikmin 2 a Blowhog may not fire when only a leader is close to it.

sections.name: Wollywog (white)
sections.card:
Summary: A large, flat, white frog found underground, called the Wollyhop on the wiki and the Wollywog in some games and regions. It is passive until a leader or Pikmin comes close, then leaps and lands on them, and the landing kills every Pikmin within a wide radius.
Weak points: Purple Pikmin slams do large damage and may briefly stun it. Swarming works less well in Pikmin 2 than in the first game, so throw Pikmin onto it instead of sending them all in.
Tips: When it is in the air, whistle your Pikmin off before it lands, so they do not fly off and possibly lose their maturity. Even a Wollywog killed as it is about to fall still crushes the Pikmin under it.

sections.name: Ultra-spicy spray
sections.card:
Summary: The red spray, made by gathering ten ultra-spicy berries from Burgeoning Spiderworts or from a concentrated dose of spray nectar. In Pikmin 2 it makes every Pikmin in the current leader's squad faster and quicker at its jobs for 40 seconds, however far away they are.
Uses: Sprayed Pikmin run nearly as fast as flowered White Pikmin and work faster: they attack more often and tear down gates, build bridges and get up from knockdowns quicker. In Pikmin 2 the leaf, bud or flower is replaced by a flashing pink light rather than turning into a flower, and they carry as if flowered, so spraying a squad that is already all flowers is a waste. Their attack power becomes the same for every colour, so Purple Pikmin hit weaker while sprayed. A Pikmin that jumps at its target before hitting, instead of latching on, is not sped up.
Tips: Spraying already-spicy Pikmin restarts the 40 seconds, and so does an ultra-bitter spray. Pikmin that go into an Onion or the ship lose the effect, and Pikmin that are drowning die faster. If it wears off while Pikmin are carrying something they keep the powered-up carrying speed until they deliver it or drop it, which helps with the Doomsday Apparatus. The Awakening Wood is the place to gather lots of berries. If no Pikmin could benefit, the spray cannot be used and no dose is spent.

sections.name: Ultra-bitter spray
sections.card:
Summary: The purple spray, made from ten purple Burgeoning Spiderwort berries or found as a concentrated dose. Any enemy or bomb rock in the direction of your cursor is immobilized and slowly turns to stone for about nine seconds: one second for the stone to form and eight of full encasement.
Uses: Petrifying an enemy that is eating Pikmin saves them, and a bomb rock in mid-countdown freezes, giving you time to run. The enemy shakes just before it breaks free. While it is stone, ordinary Pikmin attacks and leader punches do 1.5 times damage to most enemies, but only a quarter to bosses such as the Empress Bulblax, Man-at-Legs and Beady Long Legs, almost nothing to the Bloysters (0.03 times), and half to the Titan Dweevil, which can only be hurt when unarmed. Purple Pikmin stomps and bomb-rock damage are unchanged.
Tips: Aim before you press: with no enemy near, the dose is wasted. It is rarer than the spicy spray: fewer berry plants carry it, and you find it only after getting White Pikmin, near the Bulblax Kingdom. A petrified Bumbling Snitchbug drops the leader it was holding. An enemy killed while it is stone crumbles and leaves drops of nectar or spray, and a Titan Dweevil killed that way drops 10 random sprays.

sections.name: Nectar
sections.card:
Summary: A large drop of liquid that turns leaf and bud Pikmin into flowers. Any leaf or bud Pikmin that passes a drop on the ground crouches and slurps it for about two seconds, whether it was idle or sent there, and then jumps up with a flower on its head.
Uses: In Pikmin 2 one drop can be shared by any number of Pikmin, but once the first Pikmin starts drinking, the drop shrinks until it is gone when that Pikmin finishes, so only Pikmin that start drinking in that window are flowered. The window is longer in Pikmin 2 than in the first game. The best way to flower many at once is to get them to swarm in a tight group.
Tips: The wiki lists nectar weed patches, piles of rubble, eggs, Honeywisps, Mitites, Bulborb Larvae and petrified enemies among the sources; most give a single drop and sometimes more.

sections.name: Eggs (nectar eggs)
sections.card:
Summary: A white, semi-round object found in cave alcoves and a few places above ground. Attack it and it breaks open and releases nectar, or sometimes other things, including living creatures. In Pikmin 2 the eggs that Honeywisps hold work the same as eggs on the ground.
Uses: What comes out is chosen at random at the moment the egg breaks: a single drop of nectar half the time (50 percent), two drops 35 percent, a drop of ultra-bitter spray 5 percent, a drop of ultra-spicy spray 5 percent, and a group of ten Mitites 5 percent. In story mode, if the draw is a spray you have not unlocked yet, you get a single drop of nectar instead.
Tips: You can break one with Pikmin, with leader punches, or with an enemy projectile such as a Gatling Groink's mortars. A Purple Pikmin thrown at it breaks it at once and defeats any Mitites inside straight away. Using a leader is also recommended, because a thrown Pikmin that is called back may drink the nectar and waste it.

sections.name: Blue Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: The only permanent Pikmin type that can safely go into water; the other types flail in panic and drown. In Pikmin 2 five are found in the Awakening Wood, chasing Wolpoles beyond an electric gate that you break down with Yellow Pikmin.
Uses: Required: the Shower Room (its entrance is blocked by a clog underwater), the Submerged Castle (the entrance is underwater and only Blue Pikmin can enter, even with exploits), and the second half of the Valley of Repose, where Blues must destroy a white bramble gate and a clog just past the Emergence Cave; that opens the Subterranean Complex and Frontier Cavern. Only Blue Pikmin can use seesaw blocks that are underwater.
Tips: In Pikmin 2 an idle Blue Pikmin that sees a Pikmin drowning nearby runs in, picks it up and throws it to shore, unless the drowning one is too far away. They can also lift a Purple Pikmin out of water. Otherwise their attack, toughness and speed are about average, and they are more likely to die than other types in Pikmin 2.

sections.name: Yellow Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: Pikmin with large ears that can be thrown higher than any other type, which reaches high ledges and lets them latch onto the Beady Long Legs. Pikmin 2 makes them immune to electricity. Five are found in the Perplexing Pool; White Pikmin are needed just to reach them, and a Fiery Bulblax guards the entrance to their Onion.
Uses: Only Yellow Pikmin can destroy the electric gate in front of the Blue Onion, and they handle electric enemies and hazards that kill other types on contact. None of it is strictly required: no task in Pikmin 2 needs them exclusively. Their old bomb-rock carrying does not work in Pikmin 2, where bomb rocks are only a hazard.
Tips: They are recommended against a pair of Anode Beetles, which make a line of electricity that fatally shocks any non-Yellow Pikmin touching it; against Anode Dweevils, which shock every non-Yellow Pikmin under them after being attacked; and against the Titan Dweevil's electric weapon.

sections.name: Purple Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: Purple Pikmin have the strength of ten Pikmin. They are first found at a pair of Violet Candypop Buds in the Emergence Cave, where a treasure that needs 101 Pikmin to lift is waiting.
Uses: Required for the Spherical Atlas, the first treasure that opens a new area and needs 101 Pikmin, and for the Geographic Projection, which is the same; for the Professional Noisemaker, which sits inside the Waterwraith; and for the Doomsday Apparatus, which needs 1000 Pikmin or 100 Purples. They are also what makes the Waterwraith vulnerable. The best place to get that many is the Subterranean Complex: on sublevel 8, use the Queen Candypop Buds first and then the Violet ones to make 15 Purples and 2 of another type.
Tips: Their landing thump stuns most enemies one time in three, for five seconds, and a small homing steer puts them onto a nearby enemy, so the aim need not be exact. The thump kills Shearwigs and Dwarf Bulborbs, breaks nectar eggs at once, defeats Mitites in a wide radius, switches off fire geysers and electric wires, and counts as an attack against poison emitters and Fiery Bulblaxes. They do not panic at Mitites or at the roar of Emperor Bulblaxes, but they are slow, and slower still when carrying. Some bosses are harder to stun or cannot be stunned.

sections.name: White Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: The smallest and fastest Pikmin: flowered ones run at least as quickly as a leader with Rush Boots. Their red eyes let them find treasure that is completely buried underground. In Pikmin 2 you make them by throwing Pikmin into the Ivory Candypop Buds on the third sublevel of the White Flower Garden.
Uses: Needed for every fully buried treasure: no other type can do it, exploits included. They also stand through poison gas without choking, so they matter when destroying poison emitters, though other types can do it with difficulty. The page recommends them, though they are not strictly needed, against the Doodlebug, the Munge Dweevil and the Titan Dweevil's poison weapon, and for treasures behind poison-emitter gates such as the Seed of Greed, the Anti-hiccup Fungus and the Geographic Projection.
Tips: If an enemy eats one, it ejects poison that hurts the eater at once, often enough to kill a small enemy like a Dwarf Orange Bulborb, but the Pikmin still dies, so keep that as a last resort. Their attack power matches the standard types in Pikmin 2.

sections.name: Red Pikmin
sections.card:
Summary: The first Pikmin type found in every game, with sharp, pointy noses that give them 1.5 times the attack power of most types, and immune to fire. In Pikmin 2 the first Red Pikmin are five fighting a Dwarf Red Bulborb in the Valley of Repose, right next to where Olimar lands.
Uses: No task in Pikmin 2 needs Red Pikmin specifically, but until another type is found they are required by default. They are intended for the Fiery Bulblax, whose flames only they can withstand: its fire goes out if it is submerged, Purple Pikmin can hurt it with their landing, White Pikmin can be eaten by it to poison it, and in certain caves it can be lured into the abyss. They are intended for treasures guarded by a Fiery Bulblax with no water around, such as the Essence of Despair, the Frosty Bauble, the Gemstar Wife and the Insect Condo, and for carrying the Gyroid Bust through fire geysers unless the geysers are destroyed.
Tips: Their fire immunity matters less in Pikmin 2 than in other games: any Pikmin can destroy fire geysers, Fiery Blowhogs fall easily to Purple Pikmin, and Fiery Dweevils and the Titan Dweevil's flame weapon can be beaten with any type. In 2-Player Battle, player 1 gets Red Pikmin and player 2 gets Blue Pikmin with the same 1.5 times attack power.
